title: staged-gpu-onboarding-window-allocations-na-eu-apac-2026q3
content:
Summary:
This working note outlines a staggered/staged GPU onboarding plan for NA / EU / APAC for Jul–Sep 2026. Purpose is to close projected supply gaps for Q3 while preserving 15–25% operational headroom at launch and supporting soft rollouts (tiered customers + canary traffic). This is intentionally a 'windowed' plan (week-based) to allow swaps between regions and to coordinate with procurement/ops windows.

Key objectives:
- Reduce projected token-level SLO risk by provisioning additional H100/A100 capacity before major launches.
- Protect latency-sensitive routes by reserving burst pools (cold/warm standby).
- Stage region onboarding over 6 weeks per region with smoke tests and 3-step traffic ramp.
- Keep per-region utilization targets: 60% steady-state (prod), 75% peak with autoscaling buffers.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Current baseline (2026-06-01): NA=640 A100-80GB equiv, EU=320 A100 equiv, APAC=160 L4-equiv for inference.
- New procurement arrivals: 120 H100 equivalent units across July–Aug (phased), plus 200 L4 class for APAC edge in August.
- Average token mix growth +25% by September if feature launch occurs.
- Canary traffic limited to 2% initial, doubling weekly during staged rollout.

Quick gap table (high-level):
Region | baseline equiv GPUs | target equiv GPUs (by 2026-09-30) | delta | target steady util | headroom (pct)
NA     | 640                 | 880                               | +240  | 60%                | 20%
EU     | 320                 | 440                               | +120  | 60%                | 18%
APAC   | 160                 | 360                               | +200  | 55%                | 25%
Notes: "equiv GPUs" consolidates different SKUs via baseline perf index (H100=1.6, A100-80=1.0, L4=0.25). APAC target intentionally higher relative uplift to support edge-limited customers and burst pools.

Staggered onboarding windows (proposed):
- NA Window A (soft): 2026-07-06 -> 2026-07-19 (weeks 1–2). Deliver: +80 H100-equiv (mix of H100 & A100), create burst pool 40 units. Tasks: provisioning, switch fabric tests, KV cache warmup, smoke perf runs.
- NA Window B (scale): 2026-07-20 -> 2026-08-09 (weeks 3–5). Deliver additional +160 equiv, enable 50% canary ramp for lower-latency routes, route policies applied.
- EU Window (compact): 2026-08-03 -> 2026-08-23 (weeks 5–7 overlapped with NA scale). Deliver +120 equiv, run inter-region failover drills, adjust routing weights.
- APAC Window (edge-heavy): 2026-08-17 -> 2026-09-06 (weeks 7–9). Deliver +200 L4-equivalent (mix), bring up local burst caches, enable geo-fallback lanes.

Rollout policy/traffic gating (per-window):
1) Preflight: infra smoke tests, model correctness checks against gold prompt set, baseline latency check (< target +10%).
2) Canary 2% traffic for 48 hours -> 4% for 72 hours -> 8% for 72 hours. If error ratio >0.5% or 95th latency breach, immediate rollback to previous model/variant and escalate.
3) Scale to 25% then to 100% over next 7–10 days while monitoring quality/regressions.

Customer segmentation and reservation buckets:
- Enterprise Reserved (Tier 1): up to 30% of new NA capacity reserved for enterprise customers with committed SLAs.
- PLG / Free Tier (Tier 3): routed to lower-cost variants and subject to throttling when utilization >70%.
- Burst Pool: 10–15% of each region's new capacity kept for short-lived spikes; automatic reclamation after 30 minutes.

Utilization modeling (simple):
- Baseline token demand projected per region by week. If steady-state demand growth exceeds 18% week-over-week after canary, shift next window up by one week.
- Desired operating band: 40–65% avg, with scheduled nightly consolidation jobs to drop below 40% for maintenance windows.

Risk matrix (top items):
- Supply delay (HW shipping delay): mitigations = validate alternate suppliers, enable cross-region borrowing lane (costly egress).
- Unexpected model reg performance: mitigations = rollback, route to smaller quantized variant, invoke quality/regression alert.
- Network fabric flakiness during scale: mitigations = staged network tests, extra padding on DNS TTLs, temporary routing via dedicated VPC peering.

Cost / Unit considerations (rough):
- H100 equiv incremental monthly run cost per unit (est): $2,500–$3,100 (includes infra, power, infra ops).
- L4 equiv unit (APAC edge) monthly est: $350–$450.
- Cost savings lever: more aggressive KV caching (expected 12–18% token reduction for chat-heavy flows).

Action items (owner / due):
- Confirm procurement ETA with vendor group (Jorge Alvarez) / due 2026-06-11.
- Finalize regional rack mapping and cross-zone peering (SRE lead: Daniel Park) / due 2026-06-18.
- Create canary prompt set and acceptance thresholds (Applied ML: Priya S. Nair) / due 2026-06-22.
- Update routing policy docs and traffic weight templates (Infra docs: Amelia Chen) / due 2026-06-25.

Monitoring & checkpoints:
- Daily check-ins during each window (standup 09:30 PT) with infra, SRE, applied-ml, and product.
- Smoke metric dashboard to include: 95th latency by route, error ratio, token/sec per GPU, KV cache hit ratio.
- Post-window retrospective within 72 hours of window close. Capture actionables into INFR board.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Approve holding 30% of NA new capacity for enterprise reservations? (cost vs SLA tradeoff).
- Cross-region borrowing cost cap: what is acceptable monthly ceiling?
- Are we comfortable with APAC L4-heavy strategy vs shipping additional A100s (latency vs perf tradeoffs)?

Appendix (model mapping reference):
- H100 equiv = 1.6 * A100-80 perf. Use index to convert historical throughput metrics for planning.
- L4 equiv = 0.25 * A100-80 perf. Use for edge cost modeling and warm cache sizing.

This doc is a working draft for ENG-OPS review. Once approved, we will translate windows into provisioning tickets, adjust budgets in finance, and schedule the launch freeze windows in product calendar.
